rv.q: In a tour de force of wild-eyed demonic intensity, the actor brilliantly charts the evolution of an absurd upstart into blood-freezing demagogue.
Goodman is magnificent in the central role.
It is Henry Goodman’s astonishing performance as Arturo himself that really makes this production.
A truly thought provoking, intelligent piece of theatre.
It's an evening of genuinely epic entertainment.

The comic moments work and it's always a pleasure to listen to George Tabori's translation as revised by Alistair Beaton, but – pace Goodman’s neatly delivered little envoi once he’s removed the moustache – there's no horror in the heart of this farce.

cn.t: Critics largely praise Henry Goodman's bravura performance in this sharp Brechtian satire, with most finding the production's dark comedy compelling. One dissenting voice questions the dramatic transformation, but the consensus leans strongly positive.
